differsFromNord10: Read from both sources: the NORD-100 bus shares 24 lines between address and data (BD0-23 with BAPR/BDAP) and uses the BDRY/BINACK handshake; the NORD-10 I/O positions have separate BA0-BA17 and BD0-BD15 lines and different pin numbers. The two buses are not interchangeable.

disagreements.value: NDInsight ND-100-BUS-C-CONNECTOR.md differs from the 1980 table image in these source/used cells (image value first): a18 BINPUT used CM vs C; a19 BDRY used CI vs C; a22 INIDENT used I vs CI; a28 +12V used CI vs CMI; a30 used CM vs CMI; a32 GND used CMI vs --; b13 RESTART used C vs I; b14 RUN source C used I vs source I used C (the ND text says RUN is generated by the CPU); b19 BINACK used I vs C; b23 BMINH used CM vs CMI; b29 used CI vs CMI; b30 used CM vs CMI; c1/c2 blank vs P/CMI; c18 BDAP used MI vs CI; c20 BMEM source C used MI vs CMI/CMI; c22 OUTIDENT used I vs CI; c26 used I vs P; c27 used CMI vs CI; c28 used CI vs P; c29 used CI vs P; c30 used CM vs P. Signal names and pin positions agree everywhere.
